findings.message: Tool results are skipped by raw id membership in preservedLatestToolCallIds regardless of position, so an older toolResult whose raw id matches a latest-turn tool call is left unrewritten while its own (older) assistant tool call is rewritten. The history comes from a provider that reuses ids per turn (e.g. `call_0` every turn), and then the session switches to github-copilot Claude. Older assistant `call_0` gets rewritten to `call0`, but the older toolResult with `call_0` keeps its raw id because the latest assistant also has `call_0`. The result is an orphaned tool_result/tool_use pair, which pairing repair then drops or the provider rejects. The check should only apply to toolResults after latestAssistantIndex.

The preserved latest-turn tool call ids are never added to `used`, so makeUniqueToolId can map an older id to a value that equals one of the preserved raw ids, which produces duplicate tool_use ids in one request. An older assistant turn has id `call_abc`, which sanitizes to `callabc`, and the latest preserved assistant turn has the raw id `callabc`. Both end up in the transcript as `callabc`, so tool results become ambiguous and Anthropic-style endpoints reject duplicate tool_use ids. Seeding `used` with the preserved ids (and mapping them to themselves) avoids this.
